senses.definition_en: to mess up; slip up; screw up, to put one's foot in one's mouth

examples.english: I didn't want to screw up, but I ended up forgetting about his birthday.
examples.text: No quería meter la pata, pero terminé olvidándome de su cumpleaños.
examples.translation: I didn't want to screw up, but I ended up forgetting about his birthday.

examples.english: I messed up in the meeting by saying something inappropriate and everyone went silent.
examples.text: Metí la pata en la reunión al decir algo inapropiado y todos se quedaron en silencio.
examples.translation: I messed up in the meeting by saying something inappropriate and everyone went silent.

examples.english: He always makes mistakes when he tries to make jokes; nobody understands them.
examples.text: Siempre mete la pata cuando intenta hacer bromas; nadie las entiende.
examples.translation: He always makes mistakes when he tries to make jokes; nobody understands them.

glosses: to mess up; slip up; screw up, to put one's foot in one's mouth

examples.text: Estos suelos responden a una buena labranza y el perfil permite el arado profundo para aerar los horizontes superficiales.
examples.translation: These soils respond to good tillage and the profile allows deep plowing to aerate the surface horizons.

examples.english: Lift the lid (2) and let the product aerate with the fan on for 10 minutes or more.
examples.ref: 1986, Programa de Fomento Ganadero y Sanidad Agropecuaria, Panamá, IICA, page 38:
examples.text: Levantar la tapadera (2) y dejar aerar el producto con el ventilador encendido durante 10 minutos o más.
examples.translation: Lift the lid (2) and let the product aerate with the fan on for 10 minutes or more.

glosses: to air (bring something into contact with the air)
